correctness.rationale: PASS: Geometric series verifies derivative coefficients c0=1, c_k=1 before N, c_k=2 afterward. If N=1, F' has positive real part; if p=1,2, phi_p'=1/(1-z^p) is derivative of a convex map because Re(1+p z^p/(1-z^p))>0, and Re(F'/phi_p')=Re(1+z^{pN})>0. For p≥3,N≥2, the two consecutive numerator boundary zeros at alpha=π/(pN) and beta=3π/(pN) occur strictly in a pole-free sector; unwrapped argument of zF'(z) loses π at each, between smooth slope L=1+p(N-1)/2. For exact eta=(1-2/p)π/(4NL), selected arc has limiting turn -π-(1-2/p)π/(2N)<-π, contradicting Kaplan necessary condition at sufficiently large r<1. Independently checked exact symbolic formula and finite-radius unwrapped turns for (3,2),(4,3),(7,5); finite samples are only corroboration.
